title: Mate invertibility for a normalized uniformizer square
statement: For the data of the uniformizer quotient and any full-unit-normalized RestrictionSquare supplied by lem-diagonal-uniformizer-restriction-square, the scalar mate of that square is an isomorphism at every unbounded integral derived object K on X.

proof.text: Use transparent aliases for the original derived model, normalized square and all-complex mate predicate, to share category instances. Construct the rank-one short exact condensed point resolution of the actual uniformizer quotient. Its first two terms are the regular integral module; identify each with its Fin 1 biproduct.
Bundle quotientMap as a commutative ring-object map and apply the finite-free point-resolution scalar-mate theorem to the supplied normalized RestrictionSquare, its integral model R, and each K.

mathlib_searches.results: Existing declarations provide the finite perfect-model and universal-unit APIs, but no concrete quotient square theorem.
mathlib_searches.verdict: No direct existing theorem; split the two missing components.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonal_uniformizer_restriction_mate_isIso
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l)
    (π : PadicAlgCl.integers l E)
    (hπ : Ideal.span {π} = IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (PadicAlgCl.integers l E)) (n : ℕ)
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (R : ScalarRightDerived (Profinite.padicIntegersRingObj.{u} l E.1) f)
    (square : CanonicalScalarSquare (quotientMap l E π n) f R) :
    ScalarMateIsIso (quotientMap l E π n) square
lean.note: Transparent ScalarRightDerived, CanonicalScalarSquare, and ScalarMateIsIso aliases preserve the expanded statement definitionally while sharing its category instances.
